question: The narrator's description in the fifth paragraph of a sentence "assembled and ready in her mouth" chiefly serves to:

options.A: establish that Ines resents being supervised by a mate who is only a few years older than she is, and that she is about to say so.
options.B: mark the moment at which Ines sets aside her defence of her record and asks for instruction instead.
options.C: explain why Ines has not fallen or dropped a line in two months.
options.D: show that Ines has been rehearsing complaints about the crew throughout the autumn.

question: The author regards the six-year queue for a pitch as:

options.A: not a fault the arrangement has developed but a direct product of how it works.
options.B: evidence that demand for pitches has outgrown what four blocks can hold.
options.C: the one feature of the market that the 2011 permits successfully repaired.
options.D: a waiting period the Wednesday board imposes on vendors who arrive late.

question: According to Passage A, the larvae's light functions primarily to:

options.A: light the threads so that the larva can find its own snare in the dark.
options.B: warn other larvae away from an occupied stretch of ceiling.
options.C: draw flying insects into the beaded threads hanging beneath it.
options.D: signal to adults of the species emerging from the water below.

question: According to the second paragraph, printed pages are difficult evidence because the form on the page records:

options.A: one size that the punchcutter intended to be scaled to all the others.
options.B: the absorbency of the paper rather than any property of the metal type.
options.C: a punch that had been recut several times over the life of the book.
options.D: the letter together with the effects of ink, pressure and damp paper.
